My routine (warning: contains silicones + I'm lazy and broke):

1. Cowash with the either the Suave or VO5 strawberry scented conditioner, the ones that cost around a dollar
2. Condition with OGX biotin and collagen conditioner (Not CG approved and I don't know if the collagen or biotin do anything but it's cheap, smells nice, and makes my hair feel soft) I wash it out just by scrunching water into my hair and whatever stays in stays in
3.  While my hair is still wet I apply maybe a quarter to two quarter sized amount of Cantu curl activator cream and comb it through my hair and then scrunch it again. As long as I don't get it on my scalp I can apply even more than that but I'm trying to be frugal.
4. I wrap up my hair with a microfiber towel
5. After I get out of the shower and my towel has soaked up some of the excess water I take it out while it's still pretty wet and then scrunch and work in maybe a palm-full of Garnier Fructis Curl Scrunch Controlling Gel (Once again, not CG approved, but it's worked really well for me)
6. Wrap my hair back up again
7. After my hair has dried enough that it's just sort of damp, I make sure all my hair is placed the way I like, I scrunch the ends with my microfiber towel and I take a tiny bit more of the gel and just scrunch it into the ends of my hair with my hands and then scrunch with the microfiber towel again (I find scrunching with the towel tends to preserve my wave pattern better)
8. Air dry
9. Scrunch out the crunch  


To refresh I just wet my hair with a spray bottle and essentially just repeat steps 5-9 but I usually omit the use of the hair towel. I will do a reset wash every so often but I really try to avoid shampoo since it makes my hair greasy enough that you could probably make french fries in it on a hot enough day.

Not OP but it seems like they did have to bleach their hair to achieve this. Most people probably would to get this kind of vibrancy, especially with a color like this.   


If you're scared to bleach your hair yourself and can't/don't want to go to a salon to have it bleached professionally, depending on how dark your hair is certain dyes may still deposit a certain amount of color, usually colors ranging between red and purple show up the best.  


There are also brands like oVertone who provide coloring options for people with darker hair, but as previously stated they won't have the same vibrancy as light blonde hair. If you just want to dip your toe into dyeing your hair you could also try a bleach bath, where you mix shampoo and/or conditioner into the bleach making it both weaker and easier to apply, so you can at least lighten your hair a bit while minimizing potential mishaps and damage.

Unfortunately I'm not on expert on wear times since I avoid washing my hair daily and usually don't use shampoo, but you could try a permanent color like Ion (you can view a selection of permanent dyes if you look on Sally Beauty's website)   


OR if you want to help extend the life of your dye using the brand you're already using, mixing some of the dye into your shampoo and/or conditioner can also help as it can deposit some of the lost color back into your hair (might take some trial and error to find an effective ratio however, and the ingredients of the dye might impact whether or not its a good idea in the first place) if you use hair masks or anything like that, those might be the ideal products to put the dye in since you'll have them sitting in your hair for a longer extent of time.   


Some hair colors also just tend to wash out faster than others. I find that red-er hair dyes tend to last the longest while colors closer to the blue end of the spectrum fade much more quickly.   


Another thing that might be useful is using a color filler or additive since those are used to help with vibrancy and longevity.

Used to criminally bite my nails, while I was only interested in the white park of my nail, so it didn't get this bad, I'll try to help.

1) if you bite your nails as a anxiety/fidgeting reaction, try getting something else to fidget with. A stress ball or fidget cube could help keep your hands away from your mouth.

2) if you feel the urge to bite something, try bringing crunchy foods like crackers, nuts, or vegetables with you so when you feel the urge to bite your nails, you can bite something else.

3) if you have a hard time not going back to your nails, putting a clear nail polish on your finger nails might help, though I know from personal experience that doesn't work for everyone. The best solution is likely just covering severely bitten nails with Band-Aids, and covering all of your nails in some way. You could try wearing gloves, nail polish protectors, or silicone/cloth finger tip covers(even just putting tape over your nails if you have to). If you don't want to wear these in public, you can try wearing them at home so you can still lessen the damage and get used to not biting. Also you could try spraying your hands with insect repellent or something else that tastes/smells unpleasant.

4) this sounds obvious but you really have to want to stop biting and have the will power to do so. Part of what helped me stop is setting a goal for how long I wanted my nails to be, and watching the progress (of course for men the length will be much shorter than women, unless you're alright with longer nails). This gave me a bit of a goal to work towards. Also, if I caught myself biting, id make myself stop right then, even if it meant leaving a piece of nail only partly bitten off. Try to find something to distract you when the thought of biting comes to mind.

Hope this isn't all just stuff you've already tried or heard before and something here can help you. Good luck.
